title: The gas-spring branch: pitch plate connection back to the hub A datum (millimetres)

provenance.why_this_study_exists: One of the four grounded loops the pitch-system graph closes, summed on its own so that the parallel path is a first-class object a human can look at rather than an implication of the graph. Nothing here compares it to the pitch-link path, and nothing decides which of the two binds -- that is the mechanics question the tool does not answer.
provenance.signs_go_both_ways: This is the study to read for how orientation becomes sign: the four edges out from the pitch plate to the hub top deck are traversed with their orientation (+1), and the three hub edges are traversed against theirs (-1), because the hub's dimensions are authored A-datum-outward and this chain arrives from the far end. No sign is written in this file.

notes: A MILLIMETRE study, deliberately, even though the quantity anyone cares about downstream is an angle. The source sheet places the gas-spring and tangential-link rows in its TANGENTIAL section and converts them with a third sensitivity (its D12/F12) that this topology does not declare, because that column is a finite-difference linearisation of the pitch link's geometry rather than a datum. Until that transform exists honestly, this branch sums in millimetres and says so.

What is NOT in this chain and matters most: the gas-spring bushing tipping backlash. It is the source sheet's largest single angular contributor and it comes from a RADIAL clearance acting over two lever arms, not from an axial distance along this path -- see the `properties` on `gas_spring_body_height`. A chain of axial dimensions cannot carry it, which is a finding about the schema, not about the gas spring.
